prompts.text: What's a word in your language that needs an entire sentence to explain properly in English?
Tell me about a misunderstanding that helped you appreciate how differently people use the same phrase.
You can invent one new word that everybody understands immediately. What feeling would it describe?
The phrases people borrow from other languages often reveal what their own language was missing.
Understanding every accent in one language or being able to exchange simple greetings in a dozen?
A word can sound ordinary to one person and deeply nostalgic to someone who grew up hearing it.
Have you noticed yourself speaking differently around different people without meaning to?

Describe learning the meaning of a word and suddenly noticing it everywhere.
How does the language you use change the kind of joke you find funny?
What's the kindest small gesture you've witnessed between people who didn't know one another?
A crowded waiting room has a broken ticket machine. What would help strangers organise themselves fairly?
Tell me about an ordinary conversation with a stranger that made a journey feel shorter.
Shared inconvenience sometimes encourages cooperation faster than formal introductions.
Living in a street where neighbours greet each other daily or one where people help quietly without expecting conversation?
Most city life depends on countless small agreements between people who never exchange names.
Have you ever felt a surprising sense of community during an event you attended alone?
You could introduce one tiny courtesy to make public transport more pleasant. What would it be?
Describe a time you saw people coordinate spontaneously to solve a simple problem.
What makes you comfortable asking a stranger for help with something harmless?
When you explain your life to someone new, which details do you almost always leave out?

prompts.text: Have two interests of yours ever turned out to be more connected than you expected?
You have to design an event combining music, science and cooking. What would the main attraction be?
Tell me about learning something in one subject that helped you understand a completely different one.
Some of the most interesting creative ideas arise when people from different fields compare their methods.
A conversation between a scientist and a musician or between a chef and an architect?
Different hobbies sometimes teach the same habits, such as patience, timing or careful observation.
Which two professions would you love to see collaborating on a surprising project?
You're asked to create a short exhibition connecting an everyday object with an important historical event. What might you choose?
Describe a book, film or conversation that led you into an interest you hadn't considered before.
What apparently unrelated topics do you find yourself thinking about together?
What everyday courtesy did you learn was different elsewhere only after visiting or speaking with someone?
Tell me about a cultural custom whose purpose became clearer once somebody explained its history.
You're attending a celebration where you're unfamiliar with the etiquette. What would you want your host to tell you?
Asking respectfully about a custom is usually more useful than guessing its meaning.
Learning the story behind a traditional greeting or seeing how a familiar holiday is celebrated somewhere else?
What feels obvious and polite in one setting may require a little explanation in another.
Have you ever adopted a thoughtful custom from a different community into your own routine?
You can spend a day learning about one craft tied to a local tradition. What would you ask to observe first?
Describe a time you understood somebody's perspective better after learning about where they grew up.
What questions help you learn about another culture without treating a person as a representative of everybody in it?
Why do you think some new habits become effortless while others fade after a week?
You're trying to remember to drink water more regularly. What environmental change might help more than another reminder?
Tell me about a positive habit that stuck because someone made it enjoyable.
Making a new behaviour convenient often matters more than feeling motivated on the first day.
Starting one small habit immediately or preparing a careful plan for a bigger change next month?
It's easier to repeat an action when it fits into a part of the day that already exists.
Have you ever made a routine simpler instead of adding another step to it?
A friend wants to read more but struggles to focus. What would you ask about their day before recommending a routine?
Describe a habit you stopped after realising it was no longer useful to you.
What's an unexpected benefit you've noticed from doing something consistently for a while?
What's somewhere you visit often but still notice something new about?
You must guide a visitor through a place you know extremely well without using your usual route. What do you discover?
Tell me about seeing an ordinary object under a microscope, in an old photograph or from an unusual angle.
Familiarity makes life efficient, but it can also conceal interesting details.
Looking at your city from a rooftop or exploring a detailed map of streets you walk every day?
A familiar building can appear completely different when you see it early in the morning.
What has a visitor noticed about your area that surprised you because you'd never paid attention?
You have one hour to photograph only overlooked details in your neighbourhood. What would you look for?
Describe discovering a hidden feature of something you've used for years.
Is it easier for you to notice new details when you're alone or when somebody else is curious with you?
What's something inexpensive that provides much more value in your daily life than you expected?
A town wants to make daily life easier with one affordable public service. Which would you propose first?
Tell me about learning to manage something practical through an unexpected life experience.
A good solution to an everyday problem doesn't always involve buying anything new.
A tool you can repair for decades or one that is simpler to use but needs replacing sooner?
The real cost of an everyday decision sometimes includes time, effort and attention rather than money alone.
Have you ever discovered that something you assumed was expensive was actually simple to do yourself?
You're organising an enjoyable free afternoon for a mixed group. What would you prioritise?
Describe a time choosing the less convenient option turned out to save you more than you expected.
How do you decide whether a purchase solves a problem or merely creates another thing to look after?
What causes an ordinary conversation to become unexpectedly memorable for you?
Tell me about the last time someone asked you a question you were genuinely pleased to answer.
Curiosity and patience can matter more to a conversation than knowing fascinating facts.
Two people have completely different interests but must spend an hour together. What topic might create common ground?
A conversation that wanders through unexpected subjects or one that explores a single question thoroughly?
People sometimes become more expressive once they realise nobody is evaluating their answer.
How do you recognise when someone wants to keep talking but doesn't know what to ask next?
You find yourself discussing something you know little about with a specialist. What makes the exchange enjoyable?
Describe a conversation that changed direction because somebody listened closely to one small detail.
What makes you feel that you've learned something about a person rather than simply gathered facts about them?
